**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require a settled capture for completed orders**

When a `COMPLETED` order response contains only non-settled capture rows such as `PENDING` or `DENIED`, this check accepts the response because the array is nonempty. For a locally pending order, the later missing-capture logic only handles provider status `APPROVED`, so reconciliation can finish cleanly despite PayPal claiming completion without any settled capture. Require at least one capture in a settled status before accepting a completed order.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare terminal fallback payment money before continuing**

Fresh evidence after the earlier exact-fallback money repair is that an out-of-window `completed` row behind a `REFUNDED` or `REVERSED` transaction enters this branch and then continues before reaching the amount/currency comparison below. `judgeRefundedPayment` checks the refund aggregate but never compares the parent payment's money fields, so a drifted payment row can pass when its refund ledger matches the provider total; compare the transaction and payment money before or alongside the refund-ledger judgment.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require lifecycle actions to finish before declaring parity**

When the bot is down or its queue is stalled, a settled-age cancellation, suspension, or expiry action can remain `pending` or `processing` indefinitely while access has not actually been revoked. Adding those statuses to `healthyActionKeys` makes the matching terminal provider state pass cleanly, even though this dashboard-side reconciliation is specifically intended to remain effective when the bot is the broken component. After the transition lag, only a completed action should prove fulfillment, or queue age must be checked before accepting an in-progress status.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Report over-refunded ledgers for fully refunded sales**

When a v1 sale is `refunded` or `reversed`, its refund-sibling list is unavailable and this status-only path reports only `localTotal < providerAmountCents`. If the historical local refund aggregate instead exceeds the provider sale amount, none of the subsequent partial-refund branches applies and reconciliation emits no mismatch. This can let an overstated subscription refund ledger pass cleanly; add the symmetric `localTotal > providerAmountCents` comparison for fully refunded inputs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count recent local rows for already-settled refunds**

When an older provider refund is replayed or delivered late and its local ledger row is written during the final settlement-lag interval, the provider sibling remains included because its original `create_time` is before the cutoff, but this line drops the now-durable local row. The sibling diff or status fallback then reports that refund as missing locally even though it exists, leaving a false critical alert until the next pass. Only exclude the local row when its corresponding provider refund is also deferred, rather than filtering every recently written row by local `created_at`.
